title: Exploded View of a Belt-Driven Centrifugal Fan
creator: Twin City Fan
subject: Fans and blowers: basic fan anatomy
description: Interactive exploded view of a belt-driven SWSI centrifugal fan, Arrangement 9. Explore mode opens an infobox for each of 14 parts and can assemble and explode the drawing; quiz mode hides the labels and asks 10 identification prompts with two attempts each. The drawing is a simplified schematic modeled on FanPedia page 10, not to scale.

educational.subjectArea: Mechanical equipment: industrial and commercial fans
educational.topic: Parts of a belt-driven centrifugal fan (Arrangement 9)
learningObjectives: Identify each of the 14 labeled parts in an exploded view of a belt-driven Arrangement 9 centrifugal fan when given the part's name or function.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Labeled-diagram exploration followed by retrieval practice (identify the part from a name or function)
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Explore mode with infoboxes and an assemble/explode toggle; quiz mode with 10 fixed prompts, two attempts each
keyQuestions: Which part adds energy to the air?
Which inlet part shapes the air, and which ones only connect the duct?
Which parts of an Arrangement 9 fan sit outside the airstream?
Which part would you change to change fan speed?
commonMisconceptions: The inlet funnel and inlet collar are the same part (the funnel shapes the air into the impeller; the collar is a duct connection).
The pedestal is part of the housing (it is a separate support for the bearings and shaft).
The sheave on the fan shaft is the same size as the motor sheave (their ratio sets fan speed).
assessmentOpportunities: Quiz mode score: correct on first attempt, n of 10; mastery is 9 of 10.
Summary list of missed prompts with the reason for each correct answer.
